source_text: Hunc ergo de opere meo priore contextum, in hoc secundo libro suo sibi, licet cum interpolatione, proposuit [n27] . Nam et commemoratam a me formationem corporis, et ingressum animae, quam novam in unoquoque a Deo conditam, tam ratio, quam legis sacrae Ecclesiaeque catholicae confirmat auctoritas, ut spero, arte praeteriit.
pass_a_gloss: This texture, therefore, from my earlier work he set before himself in this second book of his, although with interpolation. For both the formation of the body commemorated by me, and the entrance of the soul, which as new in each one is founded by God, both reason and the authority of the sacred law and of the catholic Church confirm, he passed by, as I hope, by art.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image
LS forma; Blaise Adam forma futuri

pass_b_english: He therefore set this continuous passage from my earlier work before himself in his second book, although with alterations (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.44–49). For he passed over, by design I suppose, my mention of the body’s formation and the soul’s arrival. Reason, the authority of sacred law, and the catholic church all establish that a new soul is created by God in each person.

choices.why: Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
